 9202         unsigned FrameSize = DL.getTypeAllocSize( 
 9203             Args[i].ByValType ? Args[i].ByValType : ElementTy); 
 9204         Flags.setByValSize(FrameSize); 
 9205  
 9206         // info is not there but there are cases it cannot get right. 
 9207         Align FrameAlign; 
 9208         if (auto MA = Args[i].Alignment) 
 9209           FrameAlign = *MA; 
 9210         else 
 9211           FrameAlign = Align(getByValTypeAlignment(ElementTy, DL)); 
 9212         Flags.setByValAlign(FrameAlign); 
 9213       } 
 9214       if (Args[i].IsNest) 
 9215         Flags.setNest(); 
 9216       if (NeedsRegBlock) 
 9217         Flags.setInConsecutiveRegs(); 
 9218       Flags.setOrigAlign(OriginalAlignment); 
 9219  
 9220       MVT PartVT = getRegisterTypeForCallingConv(CLI.RetTy->getContext(), 
 9221                                                  CLI.CallConv, VT); 
 9222       unsigned NumParts = getNumRegistersForCallingConv(CLI.RetTy->getContext(), 
 9223                                                         CLI.CallConv, VT); 
 9224       SmallVector<SDValue, 4> Parts(NumParts); 
 9225       ISD::NodeType ExtendKind = ISD::ANY_EXTEND; 
 9226  
 9227       if (Args[i].IsSExt) 
 9228         ExtendKind = ISD::SIGN_EXTEND; 
 9229       else if (Args[i].IsZExt) 
 9230         ExtendKind = ISD::ZERO_EXTEND; 
 9231  
 9232       // Conservatively only handle 'returned' on non-vectors that can be lowered, 
 9233       // for now. 
 9234       if (Args[i].IsReturned && !Op.getValueType().isVector() && 
 9235           CanLowerReturn) { 
 9236         assert((CLI.RetTy == Args[i].Ty || 
 9237                 (CLI.RetTy->isPointerTy() && Args[i].Ty->isPointerTy() && 
 9238                  CLI.RetTy->getPointerAddressSpace() == 
 9239                      Args[i].Ty->getPointerAddressSpace())) && 
 9240                RetTys.size() == NumValues && "unexpected use of 'returned'"); 
 9241         // Before passing 'returned' to the target lowering code, ensure that 
 9242         // either the register MVT and the actual EVT are the same size or that 
 9243         // the return value and argument are extended in the same way; in these 
 9244         // cases it's safe to pass the argument register value unchanged as the 
 9245         // return register value (although it's at the target's option whether 
 9246         // to do so) 
 9247         // TODO: allow code generation to take advantage of partially preserved 
 9248         // registers rather than clobbering the entire register when the 
 9249         // parameter extension method is not compatible with the return 
 9250         // extension method 
 9251         if ((NumParts * PartVT.getSizeInBits() == VT.getSizeInBits()) || 
 9252             (ExtendKind != ISD::ANY_EXTEND && CLI.RetSExt == Args[i].IsSExt && 
 9253              CLI.RetZExt == Args[i].IsZExt)) 
 9254           Flags.setReturned(); 
 9255       } 
 9256  
 9257       getCopyToParts(CLI.DAG, CLI.DL, Op, &Parts[0], NumParts, PartVT, CLI.CB, 
 9258                      CLI.CallConv, ExtendKind); 
 9259  
 9260       for (unsigned j = 0; j != NumParts; ++j) { 
 9261         // if it isn't first piece, alignment must be 1 
 9262         // For scalable vectors the scalable part is currently handled 
 9263         // by individual targets, so we just use the known minimum size here. 
 9264         ISD::OutputArg MyFlags(Flags, Parts[j].getValueType(), VT, 
 9265                     i < CLI.NumFixedArgs, i, 
 9266                     j*Parts[j].getValueType().getStoreSize().getKnownMinSize()); 
 9267         if (NumParts > 1 && j == 0) 
 9268           MyFlags.Flags.setSplit(); 
 9269         else if (j != 0) { 
 9270           MyFlags.Flags.setOrigAlign(Align(1)); 
 9271           if (j == NumParts - 1) 
 9272             MyFlags.Flags.setSplitEnd(); 
 9273         } 
 9274  
 9275         CLI.Outs.push_back(MyFlags); 
 9276         CLI.OutVals.push_back(Parts[j]); 
 9277       } 
 9278  
 9279       if (NeedsRegBlock && Value == NumValues - 1) 
 9280         CLI.Outs[CLI.Outs.size() - 1].Flags.setInConsecutiveRegsLast(); 
 9281     } 
 9282   } 
 9283  
 9284   SmallVector<SDValue, 4> InVals; 
 9285   CLI.Chain = LowerCall(CLI, InVals); 
 9286  
 9287   // Update CLI.InVals to use outside of this function. 
 9288   CLI.InVals = InVals; 
 9289  
 9290   // Verify that the target's LowerCall behaved as expected. 
 9291   assert(CLI.Chain.getNode() && CLI.Chain.getValueType() == MVT::Other && 
 9292          "LowerCall didn't return a valid chain!"); 
 9293   assert((!CLI.IsTailCall || InVals.empty()) && 
 9294          "LowerCall emitted a return value for a tail call!"); 
 9295   assert((CLI.IsTailCall || InVals.size() == CLI.Ins.size()) && 
 9296          "LowerCall didn't emit the correct number of values!"); 
 9297  
 9298   // For a tail call, the return value is merely live-out and there aren't 
 9299   // any nodes in the DAG representing it. Return a special value to 
 9300   // indicate that a tail call has been emitted and no more Instructions 
 9301   // should be processed in the current block. 
 9302   if (CLI.IsTailCall) { 
 9303     CLI.DAG.setRoot(CLI.Chain); 
 9304     return std::make_pair(SDValue(), SDValue()); 
 9305   } 
 9306  
 9307 #ifndef NDEBUG 
 9308   for (unsigned i = 0, e = CLI.Ins.size(); i != e; ++i) { 
 9309     assert(InVals[i].getNode() && "LowerCall emitted a null value!"); 
 9310     assert(EVT(CLI.Ins[i].VT) == InVals[i].getValueType() && 
 9311            "LowerCall emitted a value with the wrong type!"); 
 9312   } 
 9313 #endif 
 9314  
 9315   SmallVector<SDValue, 4> ReturnValues; 
 9316   if (!CanLowerReturn) { 
 9317     // The instruction result is the result of loading from the 
 9318     // hidden sret parameter. 
 9319     SmallVector<EVT, 1> PVTs; 
 9320     Type *PtrRetTy = OrigRetTy->getPointerTo(DL.getAllocaAddrSpace()); 
 9321  
 9322     ComputeValueVTs(*this, DL, PtrRetTy, PVTs); 
 9323     assert(PVTs.size() == 1 && "Pointers should fit in one register"); 
 9324     EVT PtrVT = PVTs[0]; 
 9325  
 9326     unsigned NumValues = RetTys.size(); 
 9327     ReturnValues.resize(NumValues); 
 9328     SmallVector<SDValue, 4> Chains(NumValues); 
 9329  
 9330     // An aggregate return value cannot wrap around the address space, so 
 9331     // offsets to its parts don't wrap either. 
 9332     SDNodeFlags Flags; 
 9333     Flags.setNoUnsignedWrap(true); 
 9334  
 9335     MachineFunction &MF = CLI.DAG.getMachineFunction(); 
 9336     Align HiddenSRetAlign = MF.getFrameInfo().getObjectAlign(DemoteStackIdx); 
 9337     for (unsigned i = 0; i < NumValues; ++i) { 
 9338       SDValue Add = CLI.DAG.getNode(ISD::ADD, CLI.DL, PtrVT, DemoteStackSlot, 
 9339                                     CLI.DAG.getConstant(Offsets[i], CLI.DL, 
 9340                                                         PtrVT), Flags); 
 9341       SDValue L = CLI.DAG.getLoad( 
 9342           RetTys[i], CLI.DL, CLI.Chain, Add, 
 9343           MachinePointerInfo::getFixedStack(CLI.DAG.getMachineFunction(), 
 9344                                             DemoteStackIdx, Offsets[i]), 
 9345           HiddenSRetAlign); 
 9346       ReturnValues[i] = L; 
 9347       Chains[i] = L.getValue(1); 
 9348     } 
 9349  
 9350     CLI.Chain = CLI.DAG.getNode(ISD::TokenFactor, CLI.DL, MVT::Other, Chains); 
 9351   } else { 
 9352     // Collect the legal value parts into potentially illegal values 
 9353     // that correspond to the original function's return values. 
 9354     Optional<ISD::NodeType> AssertOp; 
 9355     if (CLI.RetSExt) 
 9356       AssertOp = ISD::AssertSext; 
 9357     else if (CLI.RetZExt) 
 9358       AssertOp = ISD::AssertZext; 
 9359     unsigned CurReg = 0; 
 9360     for (unsigned I = 0, E = RetTys.size(); I != E; ++I) { 
 9361       EVT VT = RetTys[I]; 
 9362       MVT RegisterVT = getRegisterTypeForCallingConv(CLI.RetTy->getContext(), 
 9363                                                      CLI.CallConv, VT); 
 9364       unsigned NumRegs = getNumRegistersForCallingConv(CLI.RetTy->getContext(), 
 9365                                                        CLI.CallConv, VT); 
 9366  
 9367       ReturnValues.push_back(getCopyFromParts(CLI.DAG, CLI.DL, &InVals[CurReg], 
 9368                                               NumRegs, RegisterVT, VT, nullptr, 
 9369                                               CLI.CallConv, AssertOp)); 
 9370       CurReg += NumRegs; 
 9371     } 
 9372  
 9373     // For a function returning void, there is no return value. We can't create 
 9374     // such a node, so we just return a null return value in that case. In 
 9375     // that case, nothing will actually look at the value. 
 9376     if (ReturnValues.empty()) 
 9377       return std::make_pair(SDValue(), CLI.Chain); 
 9378   } 
 9379  
 9380   SDValue Res = CLI.DAG.getNode(ISD::MERGE_VALUES, CLI.DL, 
 9381                                 CLI.DAG.getVTList(RetTys), ReturnValues); 
 9382   return std::make_pair(Res, CLI.Chain); 
 9383 }

 9385 void TargetLowering::LowerOperationWrapper(SDNode *N, 
 9386                                            SmallVectorImpl<SDValue> &Results, 
 9387                                            SelectionDAG &DAG) const { 
 9388   if (SDValue Res = LowerOperation(SDValue(N, 0), DAG)) 
 9389     Results.push_back(Res); 
 9390 }

 9392 SDValue TargetLowering::LowerOperation(SDValue Op, SelectionDAG &DAG) const { 
 9393   llvm_unreachable("LowerOperation not implemented for this target!");

 9395  
 9396 void 
 9397 SelectionDAGBuilder::CopyValueToVirtualRegister(const Value *V, unsigned Reg) { 
 9398   SDValue Op = getNonRegisterValue(V); 
 9399   assert((Op.getOpcode() != ISD::CopyFromReg || 
 9400           cast<RegisterSDNode>(Op.getOperand(1))->getReg() != Reg) && 
 9401          "Copy from a reg to the same reg!"); 
 9402   assert(!Register::isPhysicalRegister(Reg) && "Is a physreg"); 
 9403  
 9404   const TargetLowering &TLI = DAG.getTargetLoweringInfo(); 
 9405   // If this is an InlineAsm we have to match the registers required, not the 
 9406   // notional registers required by the type. 
 9407  
 9408   RegsForValue RFV(V->getContext(), TLI, DAG.getDataLayout(), Reg, V->getType(), 
 9409                    None); // This is not an ABI copy. 
 9410   SDValue Chain = DAG.getEntryNode(); 
 9411  
 9412   ISD::NodeType ExtendType = (FuncInfo.PreferredExtendType.find(V) == 
 9413                               FuncInfo.PreferredExtendType.end()) 
 9414                                  ? ISD::ANY_EXTEND 
 9415                                  : FuncInfo.PreferredExtendType[V]; 
 9416   RFV.getCopyToRegs(Op, DAG, getCurSDLoc(), Chain, nullptr, V, ExtendType); 
 9417   PendingExports.push_back(Chain); 
 9418 } 
 9419  
 9420 #include "llvm/CodeGen/SelectionDAGISel.h" 
 9421  
 9422 /// isOnlyUsedInEntryBlock - If the specified argument is only used in the 
 9423 /// entry block, return true.  This includes arguments used by switches, since 
 9424 /// the switch may expand into multiple basic blocks. 
 9425 static bool isOnlyUsedInEntryBlock(const Argument *A, bool FastISel) { 
 9426   // With FastISel active, we may be splitting blocks, so force creation 
 9427   // of virtual registers for all non-dead arguments. 
 9428   if (FastISel) 
 9429     return A->use_empty(); 
 9430  
 9431   const BasicBlock &Entry = A->getParent()->front(); 
 9432   for (const User *U : A->users()) 
 9433     if (cast<Instruction>(U)->getParent() != &Entry || isa<SwitchInst>(U)) 
 9434       return false;  // Use not in entry block. 
 9435  
 9436   return true; 
 9437 } 
 9438  
 9439 using ArgCopyElisionMapTy = 
 9440     DenseMap<const Argument *, 
 9441              std::pair<const AllocaInst *, const StoreInst *>>; 
 9442  
 9443 /// Scan the entry block of the function in FuncInfo for arguments that look 
 9444 /// like copies into a local alloca. Record any copied arguments in 
 9445 /// ArgCopyElisionCandidates. 
 9446 static void 
 9447 findArgumentCopyElisionCandidates(const DataLayout &DL, 
 9448                                   FunctionLoweringInfo *FuncInfo, 
 9449                                   ArgCopyElisionMapTy &ArgCopyElisionCandidates) { 
 9450   // Record the state of every static alloca used in the entry block. Argument 
 9451   // allocas are all used in the entry block, so we need approximately as many 
 9452   // entries as we have arguments. 
 9453   enum StaticAllocaInfo { Unknown, Clobbered, Elidable }; 
 9454   SmallDenseMap<const AllocaInst *, StaticAllocaInfo, 8> StaticAllocas; 
 9455   unsigned NumArgs = FuncInfo->Fn->arg_size(); 
 9456   StaticAllocas.reserve(NumArgs * 2); 
 9457  
 9458   auto GetInfoIfStaticAlloca = [&](const Value *V) -> StaticAllocaInfo * { 
 9459     if (!V) 
 9460       return nullptr; 
 9461     V = V->stripPointerCasts(); 
 9462     const auto *AI = dyn_cast<AllocaInst>(V); 
 9463     if (!AI || !AI->isStaticAlloca() || !FuncInfo->StaticAllocaMap.count(AI)) 
 9464       return nullptr; 
 9465     auto Iter = StaticAllocas.insert({AI, Unknown}); 
 9466     return &Iter.first->second; 
 9467   }; 
 9468  
 9469   // Look for stores of arguments to static allocas. Look through bitcasts and 
 9470   // GEPs to handle type coercions, as long as the alloca is fully initialized 
 9471   // by the store. Any non-store use of an alloca escapes it and any subsequent 
 9472   // unanalyzed store might write it. 
 9473   // FIXME: Handle structs initialized with multiple stores. 
 9474   for (const Instruction &I : FuncInfo->Fn->getEntryBlock()) { 
 9475     // Look for stores, and handle non-store uses conservatively. 
 9476     const auto *SI = dyn_cast<StoreInst>(&I); 
 9477     if (!SI) { 
 9478       // We will look through cast uses, so ignore them completely. 
 9479       if (I.isCast()) 
 9480         continue; 
 9481       // Ignore debug info intrinsics, they don't escape or store to allocas. 
 9482       if (isa<DbgInfoIntrinsic>(I)) 
 9483         continue; 
 9484       // This is an unknown instruction. Assume it escapes or writes to all 
 9485       // static alloca operands. 
 9486       for (const Use &U : I.operands()) { 
 9487         if (StaticAllocaInfo *Info = GetInfoIfStaticAlloca(U)) 
 9488           *Info = StaticAllocaInfo::Clobbered; 
 9489       } 
 9490       continue; 
 9491     } 
 9492  
 9493     // If the stored value is a static alloca, mark it as escaped. 
 9494     if (StaticAllocaInfo *Info = GetInfoIfStaticAlloca(SI->getValueOperand())) 
 9495       *Info = StaticAllocaInfo::Clobbered; 
 9496  
 9497     // Check if the destination is a static alloca. 
 9498     const Value *Dst = SI->getPointerOperand()->stripPointerCasts(); 
 9499     StaticAllocaInfo *Info = GetInfoIfStaticAlloca(Dst); 
 9500     if (!Info) 
 9501       continue; 
 9502     const AllocaInst *AI = cast<AllocaInst>(Dst); 
 9503  
 9504     // Skip allocas that have been initialized or clobbered. 
 9505     if (*Info != StaticAllocaInfo::Unknown) 
 9506       continue; 
 9507  
 9508     // Check if the stored value is an argument, and that this store fully 
 9509     // initializes the alloca. Don't elide copies from the same argument twice. 
 9510     const Value *Val = SI->getValueOperand()->stripPointerCasts(); 
 9511     const auto *Arg = dyn_cast<Argument>(Val); 
 9512     if (!Arg || Arg->hasPassPointeeByValueAttr() || 
 9513         Arg->getType()->isEmptyTy() || 
 9514         DL.getTypeStoreSize(Arg->getType()) != 
 9515             DL.getTypeAllocSize(AI->getAllocatedType()) || 
 9516         ArgCopyElisionCandidates.count(Arg)) { 
 9517       *Info = StaticAllocaInfo::Clobbered; 
 9518       continue; 
 9519     } 
 9520  
 9521     LLVM_DEBUG(dbgs() << "Found argument copy elision candidate: " << *AI 
 9522                       << '\n'); 
 9523  
 9524     // Mark this alloca and store for argument copy elision. 
 9525     *Info = StaticAllocaInfo::Elidable; 
 9526     ArgCopyElisionCandidates.insert({Arg, {AI, SI}}); 
 9527  
 9528     // Stop scanning if we've seen all arguments. This will happen early in -O0 
 9529     // builds, which is useful, because -O0 builds have large entry blocks and 
 9530     // many allocas. 
 9531     if (ArgCopyElisionCandidates.size() == NumArgs) 
 9532       break; 
 9533   } 
 9534 } 
 9535  
 9536 /// Try to elide argument copies from memory into a local alloca. Succeeds if 
 9537 /// ArgVal is a load from a suitable fixed stack object. 
 9538 static void tryToElideArgumentCopy( 
 9539     FunctionLoweringInfo &FuncInfo, SmallVectorImpl<SDValue> &Chains, 
 9540     DenseMap<int, int> &ArgCopyElisionFrameIndexMap, 
 9541     SmallPtrSetImpl<const Instruction *> &ElidedArgCopyInstrs, 
 9542     ArgCopyElisionMapTy &ArgCopyElisionCandidates, const Argument &Arg, 
 9543     SDValue ArgVal, bool &ArgHasUses) { 
 9544   // Check if this is a load from a fixed stack object. 
 9545   auto *LNode = dyn_cast<LoadSDNode>(ArgVal); 
 9546   if (!LNode) 
 9547     return; 
 9548   auto *FINode = dyn_cast<FrameIndexSDNode>(LNode->getBasePtr().getNode()); 
 9549   if (!FINode) 
 9550     return; 
 9551  
 9552   // Check that the fixed stack object is the right size and alignment. 
 9553   // Look at the alignment that the user wrote on the alloca instead of looking 
 9554   // at the stack object. 
 9555   auto ArgCopyIter = ArgCopyElisionCandidates.find(&Arg); 
 9556   assert(ArgCopyIter != ArgCopyElisionCandidates.end()); 
 9557   const AllocaInst *AI = ArgCopyIter->second.first; 
 9558   int FixedIndex = FINode->getIndex(); 
 9559   int &AllocaIndex = FuncInfo.StaticAllocaMap[AI]; 
 9560   int OldIndex = AllocaIndex; 
 9561   MachineFrameInfo &MFI = FuncInfo.MF->getFrameInfo(); 
 9562   if (MFI.getObjectSize(FixedIndex) != MFI.getObjectSize(OldIndex)) { 
 9563     LLVM_DEBUG( 
 9564         dbgs() << "  argument copy elision failed due to bad fixed stack " 
 9565                   "object size\n"); 
 9566     return; 
 9567   } 
 9568   Align RequiredAlignment = AI->getAlign(); 
 9569   if (MFI.getObjectAlign(FixedIndex) < RequiredAlignment) { 
 9570     LLVM_DEBUG(dbgs() << "  argument copy elision failed: alignment of alloca " 
 9571                          "greater than stack argument alignment (" 
 9572                       << DebugStr(RequiredAlignment) << " vs " 
 9573                       << DebugStr(MFI.getObjectAlign(FixedIndex)) << ")\n"); 
 9574     return; 
 9575   } 
 9576  
 9577   // Perform the elision. Delete the old stack object and replace its only use 
 9578   // in the variable info map. Mark the stack object as mutable. 
 9579   LLVM_DEBUG({ 
 9580     dbgs() << "Eliding argument copy from " << Arg << " to " << *AI << '\n' 
 9581            << "  Replacing frame index " << OldIndex << " with " << FixedIndex 
 9582            << '\n'; 
 9583   }); 
 9584   MFI.RemoveStackObject(OldIndex); 
 9585   MFI.setIsImmutableObjectIndex(FixedIndex, false); 
 9586   AllocaIndex = FixedIndex; 
 9587   ArgCopyElisionFrameIndexMap.insert({OldIndex, FixedIndex}); 
 9588   Chains.push_back(ArgVal.getValue(1)); 
 9589  
 9590   // Avoid emitting code for the store implementing the copy. 
 9591   const StoreInst *SI = ArgCopyIter->second.second; 
 9592   ElidedArgCopyInstrs.insert(SI); 
 9593  
 9594   // Check for uses of the argument again so that we can avoid exporting ArgVal 
 9595   // if it is't used by anything other than the store. 
 9596   for (const Value *U : Arg.users()) { 
 9597     if (U != SI) { 
 9598       ArgHasUses = true; 
 9599       break; 
 9600     } 
 9601   } 
 9602 } 
 9603  
 9604 void SelectionDAGISel::LowerArguments(const Function &F) { 
 9605   SelectionDAG &DAG = SDB->DAG; 
 9606   SDLoc dl = SDB->getCurSDLoc(); 
 9607   const DataLayout &DL = DAG.getDataLayout(); 
 9608   SmallVector<ISD::InputArg, 16> Ins; 
 9609  
 9610   if (!FuncInfo->CanLowerReturn) { 
 9611     // Put in an sret pointer parameter before all the other parameters. 
 9612     SmallVector<EVT, 1> ValueVTs; 
 9613     ComputeValueVTs(*TLI, DAG.getDataLayout(), 
 9614                     F.getReturnType()->getPointerTo( 
 9615                         DAG.getDataLayout().getAllocaAddrSpace()), 
 9616                     ValueVTs); 
 9617  
 9618     // NOTE: Assuming that a pointer will never break down to more than one VT 
 9619     // or one register. 
 9620     ISD::ArgFlagsTy Flags; 
 9621     Flags.setSRet(); 
 9622     MVT RegisterVT = TLI->getRegisterType(*DAG.getContext(), ValueVTs[0]); 
 9623     ISD::InputArg RetArg(Flags, RegisterVT, ValueVTs[0], true, 
 9624                          ISD::InputArg::NoArgIndex, 0); 
 9625     Ins.push_back(RetArg); 
 9626   } 
 9627  
 9628   // Look for stores of arguments to static allocas. Mark such arguments with a 
 9629   // flag to ask the target to give us the memory location of that argument if 
 9630   // available. 
 9631   ArgCopyElisionMapTy ArgCopyElisionCandidates; 
 9632   findArgumentCopyElisionCandidates(DL, FuncInfo.get(), 
 9633                                     ArgCopyElisionCandidates); 
 9634  
 9635   // Set up the incoming argument description vector. 
 9636   for (const Argument &Arg : F.args()) { 
 9637     unsigned ArgNo = Arg.getArgNo(); 
 9638     SmallVector<EVT, 4> ValueVTs; 
 9639     ComputeValueVTs(*TLI, DAG.getDataLayout(), Arg.getType(), ValueVTs); 
 9640     bool isArgValueUsed = !Arg.use_empty(); 
 9641     unsigned PartBase = 0; 
 9642     Type *FinalType = Arg.getType(); 
 9643     if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::ByVal)) 
 9644       FinalType = Arg.getParamByValType(); 
 9645     bool NeedsRegBlock = TLI->functionArgumentNeedsConsecutiveRegisters( 
 9646         FinalType, F.getCallingConv(), F.isVarArg()); 
 9647     for (unsigned Value = 0, NumValues = ValueVTs.size(); 
 9648          Value != NumValues; ++Value) { 
 9649       EVT VT = ValueVTs[Value]; 
 9650       Type *ArgTy = VT.getTypeForEVT(*DAG.getContext()); 
 9651       ISD::ArgFlagsTy Flags; 
 9652  
 9653       // Certain targets (such as MIPS), may have a different ABI alignment 
 9654       // for a type depending on the context. Give the target a chance to 
 9655       // specify the alignment it wants. 
 9656       const Align OriginalAlignment( 
 9657           TLI->getABIAlignmentForCallingConv(ArgTy, DL)); 
 9658  
 9659       if (Arg.getType()->isPointerTy()) { 
 9660         Flags.setPointer(); 
 9661         Flags.setPointerAddrSpace( 
 9662             cast<PointerType>(Arg.getType())->getAddressSpace()); 
 9663       } 
 9664       if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::ZExt)) 
 9665         Flags.setZExt(); 
 9666       if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::SExt)) 
 9667         Flags.setSExt(); 
 9668       if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::InReg)) { 
 9669         // If we are using vectorcall calling convention, a structure that is 
 9670         // passed InReg - is surely an HVA 
 9671         if (F.getCallingConv() == CallingConv::X86_VectorCall && 
 9672             isa<StructType>(Arg.getType())) { 
 9673           // The first value of a structure is marked 
 9674           if (0 == Value) 
 9675             Flags.setHvaStart(); 
 9676           Flags.setHva(); 
 9677         } 
 9678         // Set InReg Flag 
 9679         Flags.setInReg(); 
 9680       } 
 9681       if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::StructRet)) 
 9682         Flags.setSRet(); 
 9683       if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::SwiftSelf)) 
 9684         Flags.setSwiftSelf(); 
 9685       if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::SwiftError)) 
 9686         Flags.setSwiftError(); 
 9687       if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::ByVal)) 
 9688         Flags.setByVal(); 
 9689       if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::InAlloca)) { 
 9690         Flags.setInAlloca(); 
 9691         // Set the byval flag for CCAssignFn callbacks that don't know about 
 9692         // inalloca.  This way we can know how many bytes we should've allocated 
 9693         // and how many bytes a callee cleanup function will pop.  If we port 
 9694         // inalloca to more targets, we'll have to add custom inalloca handling 
 9695         // in the various CC lowering callbacks. 
 9696         Flags.setByVal(); 
 9697       } 
 9698       if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::Preallocated)) { 
 9699         Flags.setPreallocated(); 
 9700         // Set the byval flag for CCAssignFn callbacks that don't know about 
 9701         // preallocated.  This way we can know how many bytes we should've 
 9702         // allocated and how many bytes a callee cleanup function will pop.  If 
 9703         // we port preallocated to more targets, we'll have to add custom 
 9704         // preallocated handling in the various CC lowering callbacks. 
 9705         Flags.setByVal(); 
 9706       } 
 9707       if (F.getCallingConv() == CallingConv::X86_INTR) { 
 9708         // IA Interrupt passes frame (1st parameter) by value in the stack. 
 9709         if (ArgNo == 0) 
 9710           Flags.setByVal(); 
 9711       } 
 9712       if (Flags.isByVal() || Flags.isInAlloca() || Flags.isPreallocated()) { 
 9713         Type *ElementTy = Arg.getParamByValType(); 
 9714  
 9715         // For ByVal, size and alignment should be passed from FE.  BE will 
 9716         // guess if this info is not there but there are cases it cannot get 
 9717         // right. 
 9718         unsigned FrameSize = DL.getTypeAllocSize(Arg.getParamByValType()); 
 9719         Flags.setByValSize(FrameSize); 
 9720  
 9721         unsigned FrameAlign; 
 9722         if (Arg.getParamAlignment()) 
 9723           FrameAlign = Arg.getParamAlignment(); 
 9724         else 
 9725           FrameAlign = TLI->getByValTypeAlignment(ElementTy, DL); 
 9726         Flags.setByValAlign(Align(FrameAlign)); 
 9727       } 
 9728       if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::Nest)) 
 9729         Flags.setNest(); 
 9730       if (NeedsRegBlock) 
 9731         Flags.setInConsecutiveRegs(); 
 9732       Flags.setOrigAlign(OriginalAlignment); 
 9733       if (ArgCopyElisionCandidates.count(&Arg)) 
 9734         Flags.setCopyElisionCandidate(); 
 9735       if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::Returned)) 
 9736         Flags.setReturned(); 
 9737  
 9738       MVT RegisterVT = TLI->getRegisterTypeForCallingConv( 
 9739           *CurDAG->getContext(), F.getCallingConv(), VT); 
 9740       unsigned NumRegs = TLI->getNumRegistersForCallingConv( 
 9741           *CurDAG->getContext(), F.getCallingConv(), VT); 
 9742       for (unsigned i = 0; i != NumRegs; ++i) { 
 9743         // For scalable vectors, use the minimum size; individual targets 
 9744         // are responsible for handling scalable vector arguments and 
 9745         // return values. 
 9746         ISD::InputArg MyFlags(Flags, RegisterVT, VT, isArgValueUsed, 
 9747                  ArgNo, PartBase+i*RegisterVT.getStoreSize().getKnownMinSize()); 
 9748         if (NumRegs > 1 && i == 0) 
 9749           MyFlags.Flags.setSplit(); 
 9750         // if it isn't first piece, alignment must be 1 
 9751         else if (i > 0) { 
 9752           MyFlags.Flags.setOrigAlign(Align(1)); 
 9753           if (i == NumRegs - 1) 
 9754             MyFlags.Flags.setSplitEnd(); 
 9755         } 
 9756         Ins.push_back(MyFlags); 
 9757       } 
 9758       if (NeedsRegBlock && Value == NumValues - 1) 
 9759         Ins[Ins.size() - 1].Flags.setInConsecutiveRegsLast(); 
 9760       PartBase += VT.getStoreSize().getKnownMinSize(); 
 9761     } 
 9762   } 
 9763  
 9764   // Call the target to set up the argument values. 
 9765   SmallVector<SDValue, 8> InVals; 
 9766   SDValue NewRoot = TLI->LowerFormalArguments( 
 9767       DAG.getRoot(), F.getCallingConv(), F.isVarArg(), Ins, dl, DAG, InVals); 
 9768  
 9769   // Verify that the target's LowerFormalArguments behaved as expected. 
 9770   assert(NewRoot.getNode() && NewRoot.getValueType() == MVT::Other && 
 9771          "LowerFormalArguments didn't return a valid chain!"); 
 9772   assert(InVals.size() == Ins.size() && 
 9773          "LowerFormalArguments didn't emit the correct number of values!"); 
 9774   LLVM_DEBUG({ 
 9775     for (unsigned i = 0, e = Ins.size(); i != e; ++i) { 
 9776       assert(InVals[i].getNode() && 
 9777              "LowerFormalArguments emitted a null value!"); 
 9778       assert(EVT(Ins[i].VT) == InVals[i].getValueType() && 
 9779              "LowerFormalArguments emitted a value with the wrong type!"); 
 9780     } 
 9781   }); 
 9782  
 9783   // Update the DAG with the new chain value resulting from argument lowering. 
 9784   DAG.setRoot(NewRoot); 
 9785  
 9786   // Set up the argument values. 
 9787   unsigned i = 0; 
 9788   if (!FuncInfo->CanLowerReturn) { 
 9789     // Create a virtual register for the sret pointer, and put in a copy 
 9790     // from the sret argument into it. 
 9791     SmallVector<EVT, 1> ValueVTs; 
 9792     ComputeValueVTs(*TLI, DAG.getDataLayout(), 
 9793                     F.getReturnType()->getPointerTo( 
 9794                         DAG.getDataLayout().getAllocaAddrSpace()), 
 9795                     ValueVTs); 
 9796     MVT VT = ValueVTs[0].getSimpleVT(); 
 9797     MVT RegVT = TLI->getRegisterType(*CurDAG->getContext(), VT); 
 9798     Optional<ISD::NodeType> AssertOp = None; 
 9799     SDValue ArgValue = getCopyFromParts(DAG, dl, &InVals[0], 1, RegVT, VT, 
 9800                                         nullptr, F.getCallingConv(), AssertOp); 
 9801  
 9802     MachineFunction& MF = SDB->DAG.getMachineFunction(); 
 9803     MachineRegisterInfo& RegInfo = MF.getRegInfo(); 
 9804     Register SRetReg = 
 9805         RegInfo.createVirtualRegister(TLI->getRegClassFor(RegVT)); 
 9806     FuncInfo->DemoteRegister = SRetReg; 
 9807     NewRoot = 
 9808         SDB->DAG.getCopyToReg(NewRoot, SDB->getCurSDLoc(), SRetReg, ArgValue); 
 9809     DAG.setRoot(NewRoot); 
 9810  
 9811     // i indexes lowered arguments.  Bump it past the hidden sret argument. 
 9812     ++i; 
 9813   } 
 9814  
 9815   SmallVector<SDValue, 4> Chains; 
 9816   DenseMap<int, int> ArgCopyElisionFrameIndexMap; 
 9817   for (const Argument &Arg : F.args()) { 
 9818     SmallVector<SDValue, 4> ArgValues; 
 9819     SmallVector<EVT, 4> ValueVTs; 
 9820     ComputeValueVTs(*TLI, DAG.getDataLayout(), Arg.getType(), ValueVTs); 
 9821     unsigned NumValues = ValueVTs.size(); 
 9822     if (NumValues == 0) 
 9823       continue; 
 9824  
 9825     bool ArgHasUses = !Arg.use_empty(); 
 9826  
 9827     // Elide the copying store if the target loaded this argument from a 
 9828     // suitable fixed stack object. 
 9829     if (Ins[i].Flags.isCopyElisionCandidate()) { 
 9830       tryToElideArgumentCopy(*FuncInfo, Chains, ArgCopyElisionFrameIndexMap, 
 9831                              ElidedArgCopyInstrs, ArgCopyElisionCandidates, Arg, 
 9832                              InVals[i], ArgHasUses); 
 9833     } 
 9834  
 9835     // If this argument is unused then remember its value. It is used to generate 
 9836     // debugging information. 
 9837     bool isSwiftErrorArg = 
 9838         TLI->supportSwiftError() && 
 9839         Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::SwiftError); 
 9840     if (!ArgHasUses && !isSwiftErrorArg) { 
 9841       SDB->setUnusedArgValue(&Arg, InVals[i]); 
 9842  
 9843       // Also remember any frame index for use in FastISel. 
 9844       if (FrameIndexSDNode *FI = 
 9845           dyn_cast<FrameIndexSDNode>(InVals[i].getNode())) 
 9846         FuncInfo->setArgumentFrameIndex(&Arg, FI->getIndex()); 
 9847     } 
 9848  
 9849     for (unsigned Val = 0; Val != NumValues; ++Val) { 
 9850       EVT VT = ValueVTs[Val]; 
 9851       MVT PartVT = TLI->getRegisterTypeForCallingConv(*CurDAG->getContext(), 
 9852                                                       F.getCallingConv(), VT); 
 9853       unsigned NumParts = TLI->getNumRegistersForCallingConv( 
 9854           *CurDAG->getContext(), F.getCallingConv(), VT); 
 9855  
 9856       // Even an apparent 'unused' swifterror argument needs to be returned. So 
 9857       // we do generate a copy for it that can be used on return from the 
 9858       // function. 
 9859       if (ArgHasUses || isSwiftErrorArg) { 
 9860         Optional<ISD::NodeType> AssertOp; 
 9861         if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::SExt)) 
 9862           AssertOp = ISD::AssertSext; 
 9863         else if (Arg.hasAttribute(Attribute::ZExt)) 
 9864           AssertOp = ISD::AssertZext; 
 9865  
 9866         ArgValues.push_back(getCopyFromParts(DAG, dl, &InVals[i], NumParts, 
 9867                                              PartVT, VT, nullptr, 
 9868                                              F.getCallingConv(), AssertOp)); 
 9869       } 
 9870  
 9871       i += NumParts; 
 9872     } 
 9873  
 9874     // We don't need to do anything else for unused arguments. 
 9875     if (ArgValues.empty()) 
 9876       continue; 
 9877  
 9878     // Note down frame index. 
 9879     if (FrameIndexSDNode *FI = 
 9880         dyn_cast<FrameIndexSDNode>(ArgValues[0].getNode())) 
 9881       FuncInfo->setArgumentFrameIndex(&Arg, FI->getIndex()); 
 9882  
 9883     SDValue Res = DAG.getMergeValues(makeArrayRef(ArgValues.data(), NumValues), 
 9884                                      SDB->getCurSDLoc()); 
 9885  
 9886     SDB->setValue(&Arg, Res); 
 9887     if (!TM.Options.EnableFastISel && Res.getOpcode() == ISD::BUILD_PAIR) { 
 9888       // We want to associate the argument with the frame index, among 
 9889       // involved operands, that correspond to the lowest address. The 
 9890       // getCopyFromParts function, called earlier, is swapping the order of 
 9891       // the operands to BUILD_PAIR depending on endianness. The result of 
 9892       // that swapping is that the least significant bits of the argument will 
 9893       // be in the first operand of the BUILD_PAIR node, and the most 
 9894       // significant bits will be in the second operand. 
 9895       unsigned LowAddressOp = DAG.getDataLayout().isBigEndian() ? 1 : 0; 
 9896       if (LoadSDNode *LNode = 
 9897           dyn_cast<LoadSDNode>(Res.getOperand(LowAddressOp).getNode())) 
 9898         if (FrameIndexSDNode *FI = 
 9899             dyn_cast<FrameIndexSDNode>(LNode->getBasePtr().getNode())) 
 9900           FuncInfo->setArgumentFrameIndex(&Arg, FI->getIndex()); 
 9901     } 
 9902  
 9903     // Analyses past this point are naive and don't expect an assertion. 
 9904     if (Res.getOpcode() == ISD::AssertZext) 
 9905       Res = Res.getOperand(0); 
 9906  
 9907     // Update the SwiftErrorVRegDefMap. 
 9908     if (Res.getOpcode() == ISD::CopyFromReg && isSwiftErrorArg) { 
 9909       unsigned Reg = cast<RegisterSDNode>(Res.getOperand(1))->getReg(); 
 9910       if (Register::isVirtualRegister(Reg)) 
 9911         SwiftError->setCurrentVReg(FuncInfo->MBB, SwiftError->getFunctionArg(), 
 9912                                    Reg); 
 9913     } 
 9914  
 9915     // If this argument is live outside of the entry block, insert a copy from 
 9916     // wherever we got it to the vreg that other BB's will reference it as. 
 9917     if (Res.getOpcode() == ISD::CopyFromReg) { 
 9918       // If we can, though, try to skip creating an unnecessary vreg. 
 9919       // FIXME: This isn't very clean... it would be nice to make this more 
 9920       // general. 
 9921       unsigned Reg = cast<RegisterSDNode>(Res.getOperand(1))->getReg(); 
 9922       if (Register::isVirtualRegister(Reg)) { 
 9923         FuncInfo->ValueMap[&Arg] = Reg; 
 9924         continue; 
 9925       } 
 9926     } 
 9927     if (!isOnlyUsedInEntryBlock(&Arg, TM.Options.EnableFastISel)) { 
 9928       FuncInfo->InitializeRegForValue(&Arg); 
 9929       SDB->CopyToExportRegsIfNeeded(&Arg); 
 9930     } 
 9931   } 
 9932  
 9933   if (!Chains.empty()) { 
 9934     Chains.push_back(NewRoot); 
 9935     NewRoot = DAG.getNode(ISD::TokenFactor, dl, MVT::Other, Chains); 
 9936   } 
 9937  
 9938   DAG.setRoot(NewRoot); 
 9939  
 9940   assert(i == InVals.size() && "Argument register count mismatch!"); 
 9941  
 9942   // If any argument copy elisions occurred and we have debug info, update the 
 9943   // stale frame indices used in the dbg.declare variable info table. 
 9944   MachineFunction::VariableDbgInfoMapTy &DbgDeclareInfo = MF->getVariableDbgInfo(); 
 9945   if (!DbgDeclareInfo.empty() && !ArgCopyElisionFrameIndexMap.empty()) { 
 9946     for (MachineFunction::VariableDbgInfo &VI : DbgDeclareInfo) { 
 9947       auto I = ArgCopyElisionFrameIndexMap.find(VI.Slot); 
 9948       if (I != ArgCopyElisionFrameIndexMap.end()) 
 9949         VI.Slot = I->second; 
 9950     } 
 9951   } 
 9952  
 9953   // Finally, if the target has anything special to do, allow it to do so. 
 9954   emitFunctionEntryCode(); 
 9955 } 
 9956  
 9957 /// Handle PHI nodes in successor blocks.  Emit code into the SelectionDAG to 
 9958 /// ensure constants are generated when needed.  Remember the virtual registers 
 9959 /// that need to be added to the Machine PHI nodes as input.  We cannot just 
 9960 /// directly add them, because expansion might result in multiple MBB's for one 
 9961 /// BB.  As such, the start of the BB might correspond to a different MBB than 
 9962 /// the end. 
 9963 void 
 9964 SelectionDAGBuilder::HandlePHINodesInSuccessorBlocks(const BasicBlock *LLVMBB) { 
 9965   const Instruction *TI = LLVMBB->getTerminator(); 
 9966  
 9967   SmallPtrSet<MachineBasicBlock *, 4> SuccsHandled; 
 9968  
 9969   // Check PHI nodes in successors that expect a value to be available from this 
 9970   // block. 
 9971   for (unsigned succ = 0, e = TI->getNumSuccessors(); succ != e; ++succ) { 
 9972     const BasicBlock *SuccBB = TI->getSuccessor(succ); 
 9973     if (!isa<PHINode>(SuccBB->begin())) continue; 
 9974     MachineBasicBlock *SuccMBB = FuncInfo.MBBMap[SuccBB]; 
 9975  
 9976     // If this terminator has multiple identical successors (common for 
 9977     // switches), only handle each succ once. 
 9978     if (!SuccsHandled.insert(SuccMBB).second) 
 9979       continue; 
 9980  
 9981     MachineBasicBlock::iterator MBBI = SuccMBB->begin(); 
 9982  
 9983     // At this point we know that there is a 1-1 correspondence between LLVM PHI 
 9984     // nodes and Machine PHI nodes, but the incoming operands have not been 
 9985     // emitted yet. 
 9986     for (const PHINode &PN : SuccBB->phis()) { 
 9987       // Ignore dead phi's. 
 9988       if (PN.use_empty()) 
 9989         continue; 
 9990  
 9991       // Skip empty types 
 9992       if (PN.getType()->isEmptyTy()) 
 9993         continue; 
 9994  
 9995       unsigned Reg; 
 9996       const Value *PHIOp = PN.getIncomingValueForBlock(LLVMBB); 
 9997  
 9998       if (const Constant *C = dyn_cast<Constant>(PHIOp)) { 
 9999         unsigned &RegOut = ConstantsOut[C]; 
10000         if (RegOut == 0) { 
10001           RegOut = FuncInfo.CreateRegs(C); 
10002           CopyValueToVirtualRegister(C, RegOut); 
10003         } 
10004         Reg = RegOut; 
10005       } else { 
10006         DenseMap<const Value *, Register>::iterator I = 
10007           FuncInfo.ValueMap.find(PHIOp); 
10008         if (I != FuncInfo.ValueMap.end()) 
10009           Reg = I->second; 
10010         else { 
10011           assert(isa<AllocaInst>(PHIOp) && 
10012                  FuncInfo.StaticAllocaMap.count(cast<AllocaInst>(PHIOp)) && 
10013                  "Didn't codegen value into a register!??"); 
10014           Reg = FuncInfo.CreateRegs(PHIOp); 
10015           CopyValueToVirtualRegister(PHIOp, Reg); 
10016         } 
10017       } 
10018  
10019       // Remember that this register needs to added to the machine PHI node as 
10020       // the input for this MBB. 
10021       SmallVector<EVT, 4> ValueVTs; 
10022       const TargetLowering &TLI = DAG.getTargetLoweringInfo(); 
10023       ComputeValueVTs(TLI, DAG.getDataLayout(), PN.getType(), ValueVTs); 
10024       for (unsigned vti = 0, vte = ValueVTs.size(); vti != vte; ++vti) { 
10025         EVT VT = ValueVTs[vti]; 
10026         unsigned NumRegisters = TLI.getNumRegisters(*DAG.getContext(), VT); 
10027         for (unsigned i = 0, e = NumRegisters; i != e; ++i) 
10028           FuncInfo.PHINodesToUpdate.push_back( 
10029               std::make_pair(&*MBBI++, Reg + i)); 
10030         Reg += NumRegisters; 
10031       } 
10032     } 
10033   } 
10034  
10035   ConstantsOut.clear(); 
10036 } 
10037  
10038 /// Add a successor MBB to ParentMBB< creating a new MachineBB for BB if SuccMBB 
10039 /// is 0. 
10040 MachineBasicBlock * 
10041 SelectionDAGBuilder::StackProtectorDescriptor:: 
10042 AddSuccessorMBB(const BasicBlock *BB, 
10043                 MachineBasicBlock *ParentMBB, 
10044                 bool IsLikely, 
10045                 MachineBasicBlock *SuccMBB) { 
10046   // If SuccBB has not been created yet, create it. 
10047   if (!SuccMBB) { 
10048     MachineFunction *MF = ParentMBB->getParent(); 
10049     MachineFunction::iterator BBI(ParentMBB); 
10050     SuccMBB = MF->CreateMachineBasicBlock(BB); 
10051     MF->insert(++BBI, SuccMBB); 
10052   } 
10053   // Add it as a successor of ParentMBB. 
10054   ParentMBB->addSuccessor( 
10055       SuccMBB, BranchProbabilityInfo::getBranchProbStackProtector(IsLikely)); 
10056   return SuccMBB; 
10057 } 
10058  
10059 MachineBasicBlock *SelectionDAGBuilder::NextBlock(MachineBasicBlock *MBB) { 
10060   MachineFunction::iterator I(MBB); 
10061   if (++I == FuncInfo.MF->end()) 
10062     return nullptr; 
10063   return &*I; 
10064 } 
10065  
10066 /// During lowering new call nodes can be created (such as memset, etc.). 
10067 /// Those will become new roots of the current DAG, but complications arise 
10068 /// when they are tail calls. In such cases, the call lowering will update 
10069 /// the root, but the builder still needs to know that a tail call has been 
10070 /// lowered in order to avoid generating an additional return. 
10071 void SelectionDAGBuilder::updateDAGForMaybeTailCall(SDValue MaybeTC) { 
10072   // If the node is null, we do have a tail call. 
10073   if (MaybeTC.getNode() != nullptr) 
10074     DAG.setRoot(MaybeTC); 
10075   else 
10076     HasTailCall = true; 
10077 } 
10078  
10079 void SelectionDAGBuilder::lowerWorkItem(SwitchWorkListItem W, Value *Cond, 
10080                                         MachineBasicBlock *SwitchMBB, 
10081                                         MachineBasicBlock *DefaultMBB) { 
10082   MachineFunction *CurMF = FuncInfo.MF; 
10083   MachineBasicBlock *NextMBB = nullptr; 
10084   MachineFunction::iterator BBI(W.MBB); 
10085   if (++BBI != FuncInfo.MF->end()) 
10086     NextMBB = &*BBI; 
10087  
10088   unsigned Size = W.LastCluster - W.FirstCluster + 1; 
10089  
10090   BranchProbabilityInfo *BPI = FuncInfo.BPI; 
10091  
10092   if (Size == 2 && W.MBB == SwitchMBB) { 
10093     // If any two of the cases has the same destination, and if one value 
10094     // is the same as the other, but has one bit unset that the other has set, 
10095     // use bit manipulation to do two compares at once.  For example: 
10096     // "if (X == 6 || X == 4)" -> "if ((X|2) == 6)" 
10097     // TODO: This could be extended to merge any 2 cases in switches with 3 
10098     // cases. 
10099     // TODO: Handle cases where W.CaseBB != SwitchBB. 
10100     CaseCluster &Small = *W.FirstCluster; 
10101     CaseCluster &Big = *W.LastCluster; 
10102  
10103     if (Small.Low == Small.High && Big.Low == Big.High && 
10104         Small.MBB == Big.MBB) { 
10105       const APInt &SmallValue = Small.Low->getValue(); 
10106       const APInt &BigValue = Big.Low->getValue(); 
10107  
10108       // Check that there is only one bit different. 
10109       APInt CommonBit = BigValue ^ SmallValue; 
10110       if (CommonBit.isPowerOf2()) { 
10111         SDValue CondLHS = getValue(Cond); 
10112         EVT VT = CondLHS.getValueType(); 
10113         SDLoc DL = getCurSDLoc(); 
10114  
10115         SDValue Or = DAG.getNode(ISD::OR, DL, VT, CondLHS, 
10116                                  DAG.getConstant(CommonBit, DL, VT)); 
10117         SDValue Cond = DAG.getSetCC( 
10118             DL, MVT::i1, Or, DAG.getConstant(BigValue | SmallValue, DL, VT), 
10119             ISD::SETEQ); 
10120  
10121         // Update successor info. 
10122         // Both Small and Big will jump to Small.BB, so we sum up the 
10123         // probabilities. 
10124         addSuccessorWithProb(SwitchMBB, Small.MBB, Small.Prob + Big.Prob); 
10125         if (BPI) 
10126           addSuccessorWithProb( 
10127               SwitchMBB, DefaultMBB, 
10128               // The default destination is the first successor in IR. 
10129               BPI->getEdgeProbability(SwitchMBB->getBasicBlock(), (unsigned)0)); 
10130         else 
10131           addSuccessorWithProb(SwitchMBB, DefaultMBB); 
10132  
10133         // Insert the true branch. 
10134         SDValue BrCond = 
10135             DAG.getNode(ISD::BRCOND, DL, MVT::Other, getControlRoot(), Cond, 
10136                         DAG.getBasicBlock(Small.MBB)); 
10137         // Insert the false branch. 
10138         BrCond = DAG.getNode(ISD::BR, DL, MVT::Other, BrCond, 
10139                              DAG.getBasicBlock(DefaultMBB)); 
10140  
10141         DAG.setRoot(BrCond); 
10142         return; 
10143       } 
10144     } 
10145   } 
10146  
10147   if (TM.getOptLevel() != CodeGenOpt::None) { 
10148     // Here, we order cases by probability so the most likely case will be 
10149     // checked first. However, two clusters can have the same probability in 
10150     // which case their relative ordering is non-deterministic. So we use Low 
10151     // as a tie-breaker as clusters are guaranteed to never overlap. 
10152     llvm::sort(W.FirstCluster, W.LastCluster + 1, 
10153                [](const CaseCluster &a, const CaseCluster &b) { 
10154       return a.Prob != b.Prob ? 
10155              a.Prob > b.Prob : 
10156              a.Low->getValue().slt(b.Low->getValue()); 
10157     }); 
10158  
10159     // Rearrange the case blocks so that the last one falls through if possible 
10160     // without changing the order of probabilities. 
10161     for (CaseClusterIt I = W.LastCluster; I > W.FirstCluster; ) { 
10162       --I; 
10163       if (I->Prob > W.LastCluster->Prob) 
10164         break; 
10165       if (I->Kind == CC_Range && I->MBB == NextMBB) { 
10166         std::swap(*I, *W.LastCluster); 
10167         break; 
10168       } 
10169     } 
10170   } 
10171  
10172   // Compute total probability. 
10173   BranchProbability DefaultProb = W.DefaultProb; 
10174   BranchProbability UnhandledProbs = DefaultProb; 
10175   for (CaseClusterIt I = W.FirstCluster; I <= W.LastCluster; ++I) 
10176     UnhandledProbs += I->Prob; 
10177  
10178   MachineBasicBlock *CurMBB = W.MBB; 
10179   for (CaseClusterIt I = W.FirstCluster, E = W.LastCluster; I <= E; ++I) { 
10180     bool FallthroughUnreachable = false; 
10181     MachineBasicBlock *Fallthrough; 
10182     if (I == W.LastCluster) { 
10183       // For the last cluster, fall through to the default destination. 
10184       Fallthrough = DefaultMBB; 
10185       FallthroughUnreachable = isa<UnreachableInst>( 
10186           DefaultMBB->getBasicBlock()->getFirstNonPHIOrDbg()); 
10187     } else { 
10188       Fallthrough = CurMF->CreateMachineBasicBlock(CurMBB->getBasicBlock()); 
10189       CurMF->insert(BBI, Fallthrough); 
10190       // Put Cond in a virtual register to make it available from the new blocks. 
10191       ExportFromCurrentBlock(Cond); 
10192     } 
10193     UnhandledProbs -= I->Prob; 
10194  
10195     switch (I->Kind) { 
10196       case CC_JumpTable: { 
10197         // FIXME: Optimize away range check based on pivot comparisons. 
10198         JumpTableHeader *JTH = &SL->JTCases[I->JTCasesIndex].first; 
10199         SwitchCG::JumpTable *JT = &SL->JTCases[I->JTCasesIndex].second; 
10200  
10201         // The jump block hasn't been inserted yet; insert it here. 
10202         MachineBasicBlock *JumpMBB = JT->MBB; 
10203         CurMF->insert(BBI, JumpMBB); 
10204  
10205         auto JumpProb = I->Prob; 
10206         auto FallthroughProb = UnhandledProbs; 
10207  
10208         // If the default statement is a target of the jump table, we evenly 
10209         // distribute the default probability to successors of CurMBB. Also 
10210         // update the probability on the edge from JumpMBB to Fallthrough. 
10211         for (MachineBasicBlock::succ_iterator SI = JumpMBB->succ_begin(), 
10212                                               SE = JumpMBB->succ_end(); 
10213              SI != SE; ++SI) { 
10214           if (*SI == DefaultMBB) { 
10215             JumpProb += DefaultProb / 2; 
10216             FallthroughProb -= DefaultProb / 2; 
10217             JumpMBB->setSuccProbability(SI, DefaultProb / 2); 
10218             JumpMBB->normalizeSuccProbs(); 
10219             break; 
10220           } 
10221         } 
10222  
10223         if (FallthroughUnreachable) { 
10224           // Skip the range check if the fallthrough block is unreachable. 
10225           JTH->OmitRangeCheck = true; 
10226         } 
10227  
10228         if (!JTH->OmitRangeCheck) 
10229           addSuccessorWithProb(CurMBB, Fallthrough, FallthroughProb); 
10230         addSuccessorWithProb(CurMBB, JumpMBB, JumpProb); 
10231         CurMBB->normalizeSuccProbs(); 
10232  
10233         // The jump table header will be inserted in our current block, do the 
10234         // range check, and fall through to our fallthrough block. 
10235         JTH->HeaderBB = CurMBB; 
10236         JT->Default = Fallthrough; // FIXME: Move Default to JumpTableHeader. 
10237  
10238         // If we're in the right place, emit the jump table header right now. 
10239         if (CurMBB == SwitchMBB) { 
10240           visitJumpTableHeader(*JT, *JTH, SwitchMBB); 
10241           JTH->Emitted = true; 
10242         } 
10243         break; 
10244       } 
10245       case CC_BitTests: { 
10246         // FIXME: Optimize away range check based on pivot comparisons. 
10247         BitTestBlock *BTB = &SL->BitTestCases[I->BTCasesIndex]; 
10248  
10249         // The bit test blocks haven't been inserted yet; insert them here. 
10250         for (BitTestCase &BTC : BTB->Cases) 
10251           CurMF->insert(BBI, BTC.ThisBB); 
10252  
10253         // Fill in fields of the BitTestBlock. 
10254         BTB->Parent = CurMBB; 
10255         BTB->Default = Fallthrough; 
10256  
10257         BTB->DefaultProb = UnhandledProbs; 
10258         // If the cases in bit test don't form a contiguous range, we evenly 
10259         // distribute the probability on the edge to Fallthrough to two 
10260         // successors of CurMBB. 
10261         if (!BTB->ContiguousRange) { 
10262           BTB->Prob += DefaultProb / 2; 
10263           BTB->DefaultProb -= DefaultProb / 2; 
10264         } 
10265  
10266         if (FallthroughUnreachable) { 
10267           // Skip the range check if the fallthrough block is unreachable. 
10268           BTB->OmitRangeCheck = true; 
10269         } 
10270  
10271         // If we're in the right place, emit the bit test header right now. 
10272         if (CurMBB == SwitchMBB) { 
10273           visitBitTestHeader(*BTB, SwitchMBB); 
10274           BTB->Emitted = true; 
10275         } 
10276         break; 
10277       } 
10278       case CC_Range: { 
10279         const Value *RHS, *LHS, *MHS; 
10280         ISD::CondCode CC; 
10281         if (I->Low == I->High) { 
10282           // Check Cond == I->Low. 
10283           CC = ISD::SETEQ; 
10284           LHS = Cond; 
10285           RHS=I->Low; 
10286           MHS = nullptr; 
10287         } else { 
10288           // Check I->Low <= Cond <= I->High. 
10289           CC = ISD::SETLE; 
10290           LHS = I->Low; 
10291           MHS = Cond; 
10292           RHS = I->High; 
10293         } 
10294  
10295         // If Fallthrough is unreachable, fold away the comparison. 
10296         if (FallthroughUnreachable) 
10297           CC = ISD::SETTRUE; 
10298  
10299         // The false probability is the sum of all unhandled cases. 
10300         CaseBlock CB(CC, LHS, RHS, MHS, I->MBB, Fallthrough, CurMBB, 
10301                      getCurSDLoc(), I->Prob, UnhandledProbs); 
10302  
10303         if (CurMBB == SwitchMBB) 
10304           visitSwitchCase(CB, SwitchMBB); 
10305         else 
10306           SL->SwitchCases.push_back(CB); 
10307  
10308         break; 
10309       } 
10310     } 
10311     CurMBB = Fallthrough; 
10312   } 
10313 } 
10314  
10315 unsigned SelectionDAGBuilder::caseClusterRank(const CaseCluster &CC, 
10316                                               CaseClusterIt First, 
10317                                               CaseClusterIt Last) { 
10318   return std::count_if(First, Last + 1, [&](const CaseCluster &X) { 
10319     if (X.Prob != CC.Prob) 
10320       return X.Prob > CC.Prob; 
10321  
10322     // Ties are broken by comparing the case value. 
10323     return X.Low->getValue().slt(CC.Low->getValue()); 
10324   }); 
10325 } 
10326  
10327 void SelectionDAGBuilder::splitWorkItem(SwitchWorkList &WorkList, 
10328                                         const SwitchWorkListItem &W, 
10329                                         Value *Cond, 
10330                                         MachineBasicBlock *SwitchMBB) { 
10331   assert(W.FirstCluster->Low->getValue().slt(W.LastCluster->Low->getValue()) && 
10332          "Clusters not sorted?"); 
10333  
10334   assert(W.LastCluster - W.FirstCluster + 1 >= 2 && "Too small to split!"); 
10335  
10336   // Balance the tree based on branch probabilities to create a near-optimal (in 
10337   // terms of search time given key frequency) binary search tree. See e.g. Kurt 
10338   // Mehlhorn "Nearly Optimal Binary Search Trees" (1975). 
10339   CaseClusterIt LastLeft = W.FirstCluster; 
10340   CaseClusterIt FirstRight = W.LastCluster; 
10341   auto LeftProb = LastLeft->Prob + W.DefaultProb / 2; 
10342   auto RightProb = FirstRight->Prob + W.DefaultProb / 2; 
10343  
10344   // Move LastLeft and FirstRight towards each other from opposite directions to 
10345   // find a partitioning of the clusters which balances the probability on both 
10346   // sides. If LeftProb and RightProb are equal, alternate which side is 
10347   // taken to ensure 0-probability nodes are distributed evenly. 
10348   unsigned I = 0; 
10349   while (LastLeft + 1 < FirstRight) { 
10350     if (LeftProb < RightProb || (LeftProb == RightProb && (I & 1))) 
10351       LeftProb += (++LastLeft)->Prob; 
10352     else 
10353       RightProb += (--FirstRight)->Prob; 
10354     I++; 
10355   } 
10356  
10357   while (true) { 
10358     // Our binary search tree differs from a typical BST in that ours can have up 
10359     // to three values in each leaf. The pivot selection above doesn't take that 
10360     // into account, which means the tree might require more nodes and be less 
10361     // efficient. We compensate for this here. 
10362  
10363     unsigned NumLeft = LastLeft - W.FirstCluster + 1; 
10364     unsigned NumRight = W.LastCluster - FirstRight + 1; 
10365  
10366     if (std::min(NumLeft, NumRight) < 3 && std::max(NumLeft, NumRight) > 3) { 
10367       // If one side has less than 3 clusters, and the other has more than 3, 
10368       // consider taking a cluster from the other side. 
10369  
10370       if (NumLeft < NumRight) { 
10371         // Consider moving the first cluster on the right to the left side. 
10372         CaseCluster &CC = *FirstRight; 
10373         unsigned RightSideRank = caseClusterRank(CC, FirstRight, W.LastCluster); 
10374         unsigned LeftSideRank = caseClusterRank(CC, W.FirstCluster, LastLeft); 
10375         if (LeftSideRank <= RightSideRank) { 
10376           // Moving the cluster to the left does not demote it. 
10377           ++LastLeft; 
10378           ++FirstRight; 
10379           continue; 
10380         } 
10381       } else { 
10382         assert(NumRight < NumLeft); 
10383         // Consider moving the last element on the left to the right side. 
10384         CaseCluster &CC = *LastLeft; 
10385         unsigned LeftSideRank = caseClusterRank(CC, W.FirstCluster, LastLeft); 
10386         unsigned RightSideRank = caseClusterRank(CC, FirstRight, W.LastCluster); 
10387         if (RightSideRank <= LeftSideRank) { 
10388           // Moving the cluster to the right does not demot it. 
10389           --LastLeft; 
10390           --FirstRight; 
10391           continue; 
10392         } 
10393       } 
10394     } 
10395     break; 
10396   } 
10397  
10398   assert(LastLeft + 1 == FirstRight); 
10399   assert(LastLeft >= W.FirstCluster); 
10400   assert(FirstRight <= W.LastCluster); 
10401  
10402   // Use the first element on the right as pivot since we will make less-than 
10403   // comparisons against it. 
10404   CaseClusterIt PivotCluster = FirstRight; 
10405   assert(PivotCluster > W.FirstCluster); 
10406   assert(PivotCluster <= W.LastCluster); 
10407  
10408   CaseClusterIt FirstLeft = W.FirstCluster; 
10409   CaseClusterIt LastRight = W.LastCluster; 
10410  
10411   const ConstantInt *Pivot = PivotCluster->Low; 
10412  
10413   // New blocks will be inserted immediately after the current one. 
10414   MachineFunction::iterator BBI(W.MBB); 
10415   ++BBI; 
10416  
10417   // We will branch to the LHS if Value < Pivot. If LHS is a single cluster, 
10418   // we can branch to its destination directly if it's squeezed exactly in 
10419   // between the known lower bound and Pivot - 1. 
10420   MachineBasicBlock *LeftMBB; 
10421   if (FirstLeft == LastLeft && FirstLeft->Kind == CC_Range && 
10422       FirstLeft->Low == W.GE && 
10423       (FirstLeft->High->getValue() + 1LL) == Pivot->getValue()) { 
10424     LeftMBB = FirstLeft->MBB; 
10425   } else { 
10426     LeftMBB = FuncInfo.MF->CreateMachineBasicBlock(W.MBB->getBasicBlock()); 
10427     FuncInfo.MF->insert(BBI, LeftMBB); 
10428     WorkList.push_back( 
10429         {LeftMBB, FirstLeft, LastLeft, W.GE, Pivot, W.DefaultProb / 2}); 
10430     // Put Cond in a virtual register to make it available from the new blocks. 
10431     ExportFromCurrentBlock(Cond); 
10432   } 
10433  
10434   // Similarly, we will branch to the RHS if Value >= Pivot. If RHS is a 
10435   // single cluster, RHS.Low == Pivot, and we can branch to its destination 
10436   // directly if RHS.High equals the current upper bound. 
10437   MachineBasicBlock *RightMBB; 
10438   if (FirstRight == LastRight && FirstRight->Kind == CC_Range && 
10439       W.LT && (FirstRight->High->getValue() + 1ULL) == W.LT->getValue()) { 
10440     RightMBB = FirstRight->MBB; 
10441   } else { 
10442     RightMBB = FuncInfo.MF->CreateMachineBasicBlock(W.MBB->getBasicBlock()); 
10443     FuncInfo.MF->insert(BBI, RightMBB); 
10444     WorkList.push_back( 
10445         {RightMBB, FirstRight, LastRight, Pivot, W.LT, W.DefaultProb / 2}); 
10446     // Put Cond in a virtual register to make it available from the new blocks. 
10447     ExportFromCurrentBlock(Cond); 
10448   } 
10449  
10450   // Create the CaseBlock record that will be used to lower the branch. 
10451   CaseBlock CB(ISD::SETLT, Cond, Pivot, nullptr, LeftMBB, RightMBB, W.MBB, 
10452                getCurSDLoc(), LeftProb, RightProb); 
10453  
10454   if (W.MBB == SwitchMBB) 
10455     visitSwitchCase(CB, SwitchMBB); 
10456   else 
10457     SL->SwitchCases.push_back(CB); 
10458 } 
10459  
10460 // Scale CaseProb after peeling a case with the probablity of PeeledCaseProb 
10461 // from the swith statement. 
10462 static BranchProbability scaleCaseProbality(BranchProbability CaseProb, 
10463                                             BranchProbability PeeledCaseProb) { 
10464   if (PeeledCaseProb == BranchProbability::getOne()) 
10465     return BranchProbability::getZero(); 
10466   BranchProbability SwitchProb = PeeledCaseProb.getCompl(); 
10467  
10468   uint32_t Numerator = CaseProb.getNumerator(); 
10469   uint32_t Denominator = SwitchProb.scale(CaseProb.getDenominator()); 
10470   return BranchProbability(Numerator, std::max(Numerator, Denominator)); 
10471 } 
10472  
10473 // Try to peel the top probability case if it exceeds the threshold. 
10474 // Return current MachineBasicBlock for the switch statement if the peeling 
10475 // does not occur. 
10476 // If the peeling is performed, return the newly created MachineBasicBlock 
10477 // for the peeled switch statement. Also update Clusters to remove the peeled 
10478 // case. PeeledCaseProb is the BranchProbability for the peeled case. 
10479 MachineBasicBlock *SelectionDAGBuilder::peelDominantCaseCluster( 
10480     const SwitchInst &SI, CaseClusterVector &Clusters, 
10481     BranchProbability &PeeledCaseProb) { 
10482   MachineBasicBlock *SwitchMBB = FuncInfo.MBB; 
10483   // Don't perform if there is only one cluster or optimizing for size. 
10484   if (SwitchPeelThreshold > 100 || !FuncInfo.BPI || Clusters.size() < 2 || 
10485       TM.getOptLevel() == CodeGenOpt::None || 
10486       SwitchMBB->getParent()->getFunction().hasMinSize()) 
10487     return SwitchMBB; 
10488  
10489   BranchProbability TopCaseProb = BranchProbability(SwitchPeelThreshold, 100); 
10490   unsigned PeeledCaseIndex = 0; 
10491   bool SwitchPeeled = false; 
10492   for (unsigned Index = 0; Index < Clusters.size(); ++Index) { 
10493     CaseCluster &CC = Clusters[Index]; 
10494     if (CC.Prob < TopCaseProb) 
10495       continue; 
10496     TopCaseProb = CC.Prob; 
10497     PeeledCaseIndex = Index; 
10498     SwitchPeeled = true; 
10499   } 
10500   if (!SwitchPeeled) 
10501     return SwitchMBB; 
10502  
10503   LLVM_DEBUG(dbgs() << "Peeled one top case in switch stmt, prob: " 
10504                     << TopCaseProb << "\n"); 
10505  
10506   // Record the MBB for the peeled switch statement. 
10507   MachineFunction::iterator BBI(SwitchMBB); 
10508   ++BBI; 
10509   MachineBasicBlock *PeeledSwitchMBB = 
10510       FuncInfo.MF->CreateMachineBasicBlock(SwitchMBB->getBasicBlock()); 
10511   FuncInfo.MF->insert(BBI, PeeledSwitchMBB); 
10512  
10513   ExportFromCurrentBlock(SI.getCondition()); 
10514   auto PeeledCaseIt = Clusters.begin() + PeeledCaseIndex; 
10515   SwitchWorkListItem W = {SwitchMBB, PeeledCaseIt, PeeledCaseIt, 
10516                           nullptr,   nullptr,      TopCaseProb.getCompl()}; 
10517   lowerWorkItem(W, SI.getCondition(), SwitchMBB, PeeledSwitchMBB); 
10518  
10519   Clusters.erase(PeeledCaseIt); 
10520   for (CaseCluster &CC : Clusters) { 
10521     LLVM_DEBUG( 
10522         dbgs() << "Scale the probablity for one cluster, before scaling: " 
10523                << CC.Prob << "\n"); 
10524     CC.Prob = scaleCaseProbality(CC.Prob, TopCaseProb); 
10525     LLVM_DEBUG(dbgs() << "After scaling: " << CC.Prob << "\n"); 
10526   } 
10527   PeeledCaseProb = TopCaseProb; 
10528   return PeeledSwitchMBB; 
10529 } 
10530  
10531 void SelectionDAGBuilder::visitSwitch(const SwitchInst &SI) { 
10532   // Extract cases from the switch. 
10533   BranchProbabilityInfo *BPI = FuncInfo.BPI; 
10534   CaseClusterVector Clusters; 
10535   Clusters.reserve(SI.getNumCases()); 
10536   for (auto I : SI.cases()) { 
10537     MachineBasicBlock *Succ = FuncInfo.MBBMap[I.getCaseSuccessor()]; 
10538     const ConstantInt *CaseVal = I.getCaseValue(); 
10539     BranchProbability Prob = 
10540         BPI ? BPI->getEdgeProbability(SI.getParent(), I.getSuccessorIndex()) 
10541             : BranchProbability(1, SI.getNumCases() + 1); 
10542     Clusters.push_back(CaseCluster::range(CaseVal, CaseVal, Succ, Prob)); 
10543   } 
10544  
10545   MachineBasicBlock *DefaultMBB = FuncInfo.MBBMap[SI.getDefaultDest()]; 
10546  
10547   // Cluster adjacent cases with the same destination. We do this at all 
10548   // optimization levels because it's cheap to do and will make codegen faster 
10549   // if there are many clusters. 
10550   sortAndRangeify(Clusters); 
10551  
10552   // The branch probablity of the peeled case. 
10553   BranchProbability PeeledCaseProb = BranchProbability::getZero(); 
10554   MachineBasicBlock *PeeledSwitchMBB = 
10555       peelDominantCaseCluster(SI, Clusters, PeeledCaseProb); 
10556  
10557   // If there is only the default destination, jump there directly. 
10558   MachineBasicBlock *SwitchMBB = FuncInfo.MBB; 
10559   if (Clusters.empty()) { 
10560     assert(PeeledSwitchMBB == SwitchMBB); 
10561     SwitchMBB->addSuccessor(DefaultMBB); 
10562     if (DefaultMBB != NextBlock(SwitchMBB)) { 
10563       DAG.setRoot(DAG.getNode(ISD::BR, getCurSDLoc(), MVT::Other, 
10564                               getControlRoot(), DAG.getBasicBlock(DefaultMBB))); 
10565     } 
10566     return; 
10567   } 
10568  
10569   SL->findJumpTables(Clusters, &SI, DefaultMBB, DAG.getPSI(), DAG.getBFI()); 
10570   SL->findBitTestClusters(Clusters, &SI); 
10571  
10572   LLVM_DEBUG({ 
10573     dbgs() << "Case clusters: "; 
10574     for (const CaseCluster &C : Clusters) { 
10575       if (C.Kind == CC_JumpTable) 
10576         dbgs() << "JT:"; 
10577       if (C.Kind == CC_BitTests) 
10578         dbgs() << "BT:"; 
10579  
10580       C.Low->getValue().print(dbgs(), true); 
10581       if (C.Low != C.High) { 
10582         dbgs() << '-'; 
10583         C.High->getValue().print(dbgs(), true); 
10584       } 
10585       dbgs() << ' '; 
10586     } 
10587     dbgs() << '\n'; 
10588   }); 
10589  
10590   assert(!Clusters.empty()); 
10591   SwitchWorkList WorkList; 
10592   CaseClusterIt First = Clusters.begin(); 
10593   CaseClusterIt Last = Clusters.end() - 1; 
10594   auto DefaultProb = getEdgeProbability(PeeledSwitchMBB, DefaultMBB); 
10595   // Scale the branchprobability for DefaultMBB if the peel occurs and 
10596   // DefaultMBB is not replaced. 
10597   if (PeeledCaseProb != BranchProbability::getZero() && 
10598       DefaultMBB == FuncInfo.MBBMap[SI.getDefaultDest()]) 
10599     DefaultProb = scaleCaseProbality(DefaultProb, PeeledCaseProb); 
10600   WorkList.push_back( 
10601       {PeeledSwitchMBB, First, Last, nullptr, nullptr, DefaultProb}); 
10602  
10603   while (!WorkList.empty()) { 
10604     SwitchWorkListItem W = WorkList.back(); 
10605     WorkList.pop_back(); 
10606     unsigned NumClusters = W.LastCluster - W.FirstCluster + 1; 
10607  
10608     if (NumClusters > 3 && TM.getOptLevel() != CodeGenOpt::None && 
10609         !DefaultMBB->getParent()->getFunction().hasMinSize()) { 
10610       // For optimized builds, lower large range as a balanced binary tree. 
10611       splitWorkItem(WorkList, W, SI.getCondition(), SwitchMBB); 
10612       continue; 
10613     } 
10614  
10615     lowerWorkItem(W, SI.getCondition(), SwitchMBB, DefaultMBB); 
10616   } 
10617 } 
10618  
10619 void SelectionDAGBuilder::visitFreeze(const FreezeInst &I) { 
10620   SmallVector<EVT, 4> ValueVTs; 
10621   ComputeValueVTs(DAG.getTargetLoweringInfo(), DAG.getDataLayout(), I.getType(), 
10622                   ValueVTs); 
10623   unsigned NumValues = ValueVTs.size(); 
10624   if (NumValues == 0) return; 
10625  
10626   SmallVector<SDValue, 4> Values(NumValues); 
10627   SDValue Op = getValue(I.getOperand(0)); 
10628  
10629   for (unsigned i = 0; i != NumValues; ++i) 
10630     Values[i] = DAG.getNode(ISD::FREEZE, getCurSDLoc(), ValueVTs[i], 
10631                             SDValue(Op.getNode(), Op.getResNo() + i)); 
10632  
10633   setValue(&I, DAG.getNode(ISD::MERGE_VALUES, getCurSDLoc(), 
10634                            DAG.getVTList(ValueVTs), Values)); 
10635 } 
10636
